options.text: An empty result from an existing table
options.explanation: The CREATE TABLE is transactional too, so the table itself does not remain.
Correct. Rolling back this supported transactional DDL removes the table created inside the transaction.
The new table has a separate name and never referred to products; rollback leaves the shop untouched.

workedExample:
1. BEGIN starts one transaction.
2. CREATE TABLE and INSERT belong to it.
3. ROLLBACK undoes both, so the name migration_probe no longer exists.
4. A subsequent SELECT raises a missing-table error. This applies to these commands in SQLite and PostgreSQL; it is not a promise about every engine or administrative command.
